tracks.narration: How do you draw a hill on a flat page? A contour map. Let us see why it works.
Here is the hill — a surface z equals f of x and y. Below it, a blank xy plane, ready to receive its shadow.

Slice the surface with a horizontal plane at height h. The cross section is a closed curve — the level set. Drop it straight down to the floor and you have one contour. Sweep h upward and the contour map fills in.
Tight contours, steep slope. Loose contours, gentle slope. The map reads height changes from line spacing.
A surface and its contour map are the same picture — one folded up into 3D, the other flat. The map is just the surface, seen from above.
